title: feat(rules): add SS-018 unchecked integer cast detector
problem: Entry points use `as` casts to narrow or convert integer types derived from storage or parameters, silently truncating or wrapping values.
why: Truncated amounts and balances corrupt accounting and can be exploited.
scope: Flag `ExprCast` on integer types where the operand is a storage read or parameter.
Ignore widening casts to the same or larger width.
guidance: Add cast facts with source/target type text to `rules::util`.
Prefer `TryFrom`/`try_into` in remediation.
acceptance: Negative fixture using `try_into` does not trigger

title: feat(rules): add SS-019 ignored cross-contract call result detector
problem: Cross-contract calls whose `Result`/`Option` is discarded let failures pass silently and continue with invalid state.
why: Ignoring a failed external call is a common source of accounting inconsistency.
scope: Flag cross-contract client calls used as statements without `?`, `match`, or `if let`.
guidance: Reuse cross-contract constructor facts; treat calls in expression position as handled.
acceptance: Negative fixture using `?` does not trigger

title: feat(rules): add SS-020 unvalidated XDR/Bytes deserialization detector
problem: Contracts deserialize attacker-supplied `Bytes`/XDR without validating length or structure before use.
why: Malformed inputs can trigger panics or unexpected state transitions.
scope: Flag `from_xdr`, `try_from`, and byte-to-type conversions on parameter-derived bytes.
guidance: Pair with a check for length or `Result` handling.
security: Medium/low; document that Soroban may reject malformed XDR before the contract runs.

title: feat(rules): add SS-021 temporary-storage-for-durable-state detector
problem: Durable data is written to temporary storage, whose entries are removed when their TTL lapses.
why: Data intended to persist can silently disappear, breaking contracts.
scope: Flag `temporary()` writes for keys that look like configuration, balances, or ownership.
guidance: Use a documented key heuristic; keep confidence low.

title: feat(rules): add SS-022 symbol_short key collision detector
problem: `symbol_short!` truncates long names, so distinct conceptual keys can collide on the same on-chain key.
why: Key collisions corrupt or overwrite state.
scope: Flag `symbol_short!` arguments longer than the documented limit or built from user input.
guidance: Document the exact length limit for the supported SDK versions.

title: feat(rules): add SS-023 sensitive-data-in-events detector
problem: Events may publish sensitive-looking values (keys, preimages, secrets) that become permanently public on the ledger.
why: Ledger data is public forever; accidental disclosure is irreversible.
scope: Flag event publishes with parameter or literal values whose names suggest secrets (`secret`, `key`, `seed`, `proof`).
guidance: Name-based heuristic only; keep confidence low and document it.
acceptance: Negative fixture with benign event data

title: feat(rules): add SS-024 missing contracttype on boundary types detector
problem: Public types returned by or passed to contract entry points lack `#[contracttype]`, causing runtime serialization failures.
why: The failure is a hard runtime error, not a compile error, and easy to miss in review.
scope: Flag entry-point parameter/return types that are local structs/enums without `#[contracttype]`.
guidance: Resolve local type names against the contracttype inventory; skip SDK types.

title: feat(rules): add SS-025 unbounded string/bytes persistence detector
problem: User-controlled `String`/`Bytes` values are persisted without a length bound, growing ledger entries.
why: Unbounded storage increases rent and can exceed limits, a denial of service.
scope: Flag storage writes of parameter `String`/`Bytes` without an adjacent length check.
guidance: Look for `.len()` comparisons guarding the write.

title: feat(rules): add SS-026 inconsistent TTL constants detector
problem: Different `extend_ttl`/`set_ttl` calls use inconsistent or extremely short/long constants, indicating accidental policy drift.
why: Inconsistent TTL policy leads to surprising data loss or excessive rent.
scope: Collect TTL constant arguments across the project and flag outliers against a documented policy.
guidance: Support a configured expected range; report the outliers with their values.

title: feat(rules): add SS-027 current_contract_address as auth subject detector
problem: `env.current_contract_address()` is passed to `require_auth`, which authorizes the contract itself rather than the caller.
why: This is almost always a logic error and defeats the intended access control.
scope: Flag `require_auth` calls whose receiver is `current_contract_address()`.
guidance: Match the receiver expression chain; provide the caller-based alternative in remediation.

title: feat(rules): add SS-028 missing reentrancy guard detector
problem: Entry points that make cross-contract calls and mutate shared state lack a reentrancy guard.
why: Soroban permits reentrancy; unguarded flows can observe or exploit inconsistent state.
scope: Flag cross-contract calls followed by state mutation with no guard flag in storage.
guidance: Recognize a documented guard pattern (a storage flag checked and set before the call).

title: feat(rules): add SS-029 test-only helper exposed as entry point detector
problem: Functions intended for tests are declared `pub` in a `#[contractimpl]`, making them callable on-chain.
why: Accidental backdoors can bypass intended access control.
scope: Flag entry points with attributes or names indicating test/debug intent (`#[cfg(test)]` is handled elsewhere; names like `test_`, `debug_`).
guidance: Name-and-attribute heuristic; keep confidence medium.

title: feat(rules): add SS-030 unvalidated token address detector
problem: Token clients are constructed from a caller-supplied address without verifying it matches expected configuration.
why: An attacker can substitute a malicious token contract.
scope: Flag `token::Client::new` on an address that is a parameter and not compared to stored configuration.
guidance: Look for a storage comparison guarding the construction.

title: feat(rules): add SS-031 user-controlled event topic detector
problem: Event topics are built from user input, letting callers forge events that look like trusted ones.
why: Off-chain indexers may trust spoofed events.
scope: Flag event publishes whose topic arguments derive from parameters.
guidance: Distinguish constant topics from parameter-derived topics.

title: feat(rules): add SS-032 redundant require_auth in loop detector
problem: `require_auth` is invoked inside a loop, repeating an expensive authorization per iteration.
why: It wastes resources and often indicates the authorization should be hoisted and bound to arguments.
scope: Flag `require_auth` calls lexically inside loop bodies.
guidance: Detect loop constructs while visiting the block.

title: feat(rules): add SS-033 wildcard SDK import detector
problem: `use soroban_sdk::*;` obscures which SDK items are used and can hide deprecated or unsafe APIs.
why: Explicit imports improve reviewability and future analysis.
scope: Flag glob imports from `soroban_sdk` in contract source.
guidance: Search `Item::Use` trees for a glob terminal.

title: feat(rules): add SS-034 unvalidated deployer usage detector
problem: `env.deployer()` is used to deploy contracts without validating the deployer identity or the resulting address.
why: Unvalidated deployment can let attackers deploy and register malicious contracts.
scope: Flag `deployer()` chains that deploy or register without a prior authorization check.
guidance: Combine with authorization facts.

title: feat(rules): add SS-035 ignored checked-arithmetic result detector
problem: The result of `checked_add`/`checked_sub`/`checked_mul` is discarded, so overflow silently produces `None` and is ignored.
why: Ignoring the checked result reintroduces the very bug the checked API prevents.
scope: Flag checked-math calls used as statements or whose `Option`/`Result` is not handled.
guidance: Look for `unwrap_or`/`?`/`match` handling; otherwise report.

title: feat(rules): add SS-036 deprecated SDK API usage detector
problem: Contracts use SDK APIs that were removed or replaced across versions, which may fail to build against newer SDKs and can indicate stale security assumptions.
why: Deprecated APIs increase the risk of silent behavior changes on upgrade.
scope: Maintain a versioned table of known deprecated API paths and flag their use.
guidance: Keep the table data-driven and documented per SDK version.
acceptance: Table documented in the rule page

title: feat(rules): add SS-037 competing authorization calls detector
problem: A single operation calls `require_auth` for multiple different actors, which usually indicates confused authorization semantics.
why: Multiple competing approvals often mask a logic error and complicate reasoning about who is authorized.
scope: Flag entry points containing two or more `require_auth` calls on distinct actors.
guidance: Compare rendered receiver text; document that legitimate multi-party flows exist.
acceptance: Negative fixture for a documented multi-sig pattern
